report:
Reviewed the complete evidence_status claim, sole ordinary browser implementation, both ordinary evidence tests and the explicit TODO test. Independently verified exact byte equality of browser.rs, evidence.rs and spec_plan.rs against the supplied historical snapshots; prior approval is baseline context, not execution evidence. Current source_data copies source snapshots and serialized RustSite locations from the correspondence inventory; captured RustSite/CorrespondenceIndex definitions explicitly distinguish textual inherited cfg and source declarations from binary presence or recorded execution. Browser serialization itself neither executes tests nor turns associations into proof. The prior rationale's reference to status serialization should be read narrowly: placeholder status is established by evidence assertions, whereas browser SourceReference contains RustSite and source, not a recorded-run result.

The full cargo_owned_out_of_line_sources_retain_inherited_module_and_cfg test asserts inventory of a cfg(any()) out-of-line module, retained cfg, TODO module/status/explanation and source excerpt, while excluding an unowned file. This meaningfully checks that inventory does not imply compilation. implementation_status_uses_module_ancestry_and_preserves_cfg_and_explanations asserts three independent entries, inherited cfg, TODO and N/A explanations, ordinary status for a function merely named todo, and absence of invented tests. Its captured index helper constructs a real CorrespondenceIndex from source. These assertions would detect dropped cfg or placeholder misclassification; they do not establish UI run/trace separation or that dummy success cannot promote an entry.

Those remaining aspects are explicitly deferred by todo::source_associations_are_distinct_from_run_evidence. Its empty body and comment are not behavioral evidence. Completing it requires recorded-run/trace evidence integration and presentation that keeps source associations separate, plus assertions that structural-check or dummy-test success leaves both TODO and N/A evidence unestablished. The TODO also retains the cfg requirement, already partially supported by ordinary tests; accepting this overlap does not claim completion. Thus every claim aspect is accounted for as source evidence or visible justified deferral, with no reclassification or requested edits.

Personally executed review start/read, exact source comparison and review record; no behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. Coordinator-reported 321 passing sage-meta tests and workspace build are separate execution context and do not establish the deferred behavior.
